findings.population: adults with symptomatic knee osteoarthritis (n=1,583, multicenter)
findings.finding_summary: In the NIH GAIT trial (1,583 patients, placebo- and celecoxib-controlled), glucosamine hydrochloride alone or with chondroitin sulfate was not effective for the study population as a whole on the primary knee-pain outcome.
findings.limitations: an exploratory analysis suggested the glucosamine + chondroitin combination might help the moderate-to-severe pain subgroup; GAIT used the hydrochloride salt, so this null does not automatically transfer to glucosamine sulfate

findings.population: adults with symptomatic knee osteoarthritis (n=1,583, multicenter)
findings.finding_summary: In the same GAIT trial, chondroitin sulfate alone was not effective versus placebo on the primary knee-pain outcome for the study population as a whole.
findings.limitations: same moderate-to-severe-subgroup caveat as the glucosamine row

findings.finding_summary: This Cochrane review (25 studies, 4,963 patients) found the Rotta-preparation glucosamine sulfate improved function (about 2 points versus no glucosamine) with no excess side effects, while analysis restricted to studies with adequate allocation concealment failed to show any benefit for pain.
findings.limitations: the benefit signal is preparation-specific (Rotta glucosamine sulfate) and weakens in the best-concealed trials

findings.population: adults with osteoarthritis (Cochrane review to November 2013)
findings.finding_summary: This Cochrane review found chondroitin may slightly improve pain in the short term (20% pain improvement in slightly more people), probably slightly improves quality of life (Lequesne index), slightly slows radiographic joint-space narrowing, and shows little or no difference in adverse events versus comparators.
findings.limitations: the authors grade the benefit as slight and the underlying evidence quality as low; contrast with GAIT's overall null is preserved in the paired row

findings.endpoint: knee osteoarthritis pain and physical function
findings.finding_summary: In this pilot randomized trial, MSM 3 g twice daily produced significant decreases in WOMAC pain and physical-function impairment versus placebo without major adverse events.
findings.limitations: pilot-scale trial; the authors note effects were modest and long-term benefit unstudied

findings.endpoint: knee-pain prevention in military initial entry trainees
findings.population: young, active military initial entry trainees
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized controlled prevention trial, 3 g/day MSM did not significantly improve knee outcomes versus placebo in young, active trainees.
findings.limitations: prevention in healthy young adults is a different question from treatment of established osteoarthritis — staged beside the treatment row so the boundary is visible

findings.finding_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of seven trials (545 patients) found Boswellia and its extracts relieved pain and stiffness with significant improvements in visual analogue scale and WOMAC pain versus control.
findings.limitations: small trial pool with heterogeneous standardized extracts and doses

findings.endpoint: knee osteoarthritis symptoms (WOMAC) versus placebo and glucosamine+chondroitin
findings.population: adults with knee osteoarthritis (n=191, three-arm multicenter trial)
findings.finding_summary: In this multicenter randomized double-blind trial, UC-II 40 mg/day significantly reduced total WOMAC score at day 180 versus both placebo (p=0.002) and glucosamine 1,500 mg + chondroitin 1,200 mg (p=0.04).
findings.limitations: proprietary-ingredient trial (UC-II); replication outside sponsor-affiliated groups is limited

findings.population: adults with knee osteoarthritis (two-site randomized double-blind trial)
findings.finding_summary: In this earlier two-site randomized double-blind trial, UC-II reduced WOMAC score by 33% at 90 days versus 14% with glucosamine plus chondroitin.
findings.limitations: small trial of the same proprietary ingredient; no placebo arm in this comparison

findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis of 11 studies found SAMe better than placebo for functional limitation (effect size 0.31, 95% CI 0.099 to 0.520) but not significantly for pain (effect size 0.22, 95% CI -0.247 to 0.693), and comparable to NSAIDs for both outcomes with tolerability similar to placebo and better than NSAIDs.
findings.limitations: a later Cochrane review judged the evidence inconclusive, hampered by mainly small trials of questionable quality
